title: Overnight Returns of Stock Indexes: Evidence from ETFs and Futures
one_line: In US index ETFs and most international index futures (1999-2014), overnight returns are positive and daytime returns negative; the overnight return predicts the first half hour NEGATIVELY and the last half hour POSITIVELY, in and out of sample.

findings.statement: Overnight returns significantly positive, trading-hours returns negative; overnight volatility lower.
findings.evidence: US ETFs and most international index futures, 1999-2014 (IREF 48).

findings.statement: Overnight return predicts the first-half-hour return negatively (open reversal) and the last-half-hour return positively.
findings.evidence: In-sample and out-of-sample; no magnitudes in the abstract.

findings.statement: Not consistent with the usual risk-return tradeoff; trading hours carry most of the risk.

why.pattern: Liquidity provision / inventory: overnight moves partly reverse at the open, then the day's direction carries into the close.
why.mechanism: Market makers unwind overnight inventory at the open (reversal); close-related flows follow the day (last half-hour continuation).

reported_results.headline: Overnight return → first 30 min (−), last 30 min (+).

tradable_edge: Supports two specs already on file: overnight_reversal_first_hour_es (fade the overnight move early) and noise_area_last_half_hour_es (last-30-minute continuation).
angles: Use the overnight return as an extra predictor/filter in both specs

decay_risk.reason: Sample ends 2014; our ES 2015-2023 is out-of-sample.

data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
